headline: Write-off of $344,339.40 in COVID disaster costs and ordinance amendment on parking citation penalties.
summary: The committee will review Finance Department reports, consider writing off COVID-related disaster costs, review monthly financial reports, and vote on an ordinance amendment updating parking citation penalties.
items: Update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund
Finance Department reports from Kim LeBlanc: Accounts Receivable over 90 days, Aging Report, Outstanding Receivables
Request to write-off outstanding invoices for COVID Disaster Costs incurred by DPW, Fire, and Police in the amount of $344,339.40
City's Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first month of FY27 from Sharon Wickens
Ordinance Amendment to Section 70.78 Basic Penalty of the Code of Ordinances to include updated parking and other citations
plain_text:
COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE 
ADMINISTRATION 
October 20, 2026 at 5:15 PM 
Aldermanic Chambers, City Hall (3rd Floor) 
 
Members: O'Neil, Terrio, Goonan, Burkush, Vincent 
 
AGENDA 
 
 
The Chairman calls the meeting to order. 
  
The Clerk calls the roll. 
  
1. Update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund. 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
2. Communication from Kim LeBlanc, Financial Analyst II, submitting Finance 
Department reports as follows: 
• Accounts Receivable over 90 days 
• Aging Report 
• Outstanding Receivables 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
3. Communication from the Financial Analyst requesting to write-off outstanding 
invoices related to the COVID Disaster Costs incurred by DPW, Fire, and Police 
in the amount of $344,339.40. 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure? 
    
4. Communication from Sharon Wickens, Finance Officer, submitting the City's 
Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first month of FY27. 
Gentlemen, what is your pleasure?
October 20, 2026 COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATION 
Page 2 of 2 
 
 
5. Ordinance Amendment: 
 
"Amending Section 70.78 Basic Penalty of the Code of Ordinances of the City 
of Manchester to include updated parking and other citations." 
If the Committee so desires, a motion is in order that the Ordinance 
Amendment ought to pass and be Enrolled. 
    
If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn.
